plainFields.description: Last update timestamp (including status or handler change).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete time (null unless deleted). For data retention & audit.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_reports
models.description: Logs each abuse report submitted against a specific comment. Stores reporter, target comment, reason, type, status, handler, result, freeform message for complete lifecycle audit. Enables tracking each reported comment's review status and moderator actions. Relates to {@link discussion_board_comments}, {@link discussion_board_members}, and moderation staff tables.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Target comment being reported. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reporting user who submitted the report. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

foreignFields.name: handler_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin or moderator who reviewed this report (if any). {@link discussion_board_admins.id}

plainFields.name: reason_type
plainFields.description: Coded reason for report (ex: spam, hate, personal info). For stats/policy classification.

plainFields.name: reason_text
plainFields.description: Freeform explanation of the report, provided by reporter.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current report status: 'pending', 'in_review', 'action_taken', 'rejected', etc.

plainFields.name: resolution_message
plainFields.description: Moderator/admin's notes or action message, shown to relevant users as needed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Time this report record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for status or handler change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete time (null unless deleted). Used for audit and regulatory compliance.

models.name: discussion_board_user_sanctions
models.description: Tracks all sanctions, bans, or disciplinary actions given to users for rules violations. Records offender, sanctioning admin/moderator, type/level of penalty, reason, timeline, and notes. Each entry supports full audit for compliance, analytics, and legal requirement. Relates to {@link discussion_board_members}, {@link discussion_board_admins}.

foreignFields.name: sanctioned_member_id
foreignFields.description: User receiving this sanction (offender). {@link discussion_board_members.id}

foreignFields.name: sanctioning_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin/moderator who issued the sanction. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}

plainFields.name: sanction_type
plainFields.description: Sanction category code, such as 'warning', 'temporary_ban', 'permanent_ban', or 'content_removal'.

plainFields.name: sanction_level
plainFields.description: Business code for severity/level (examples: 'minor', 'moderate', 'severe').

plainFields.name: reason_type
plainFields.description: Policy code for why this sanction is imposed (like 'hate', 'harassment', 'spam').

plainFields.name: reason_text
plainFields.description: Moderator/admin notes and justification in freeform text.

plainFields.name: timeline_start
plainFields.description: Sanction effective start time (UTC).

plainFields.name: timeline_end
plainFields.description: Sanction scheduled end time (null for permanent sanctions).

plainFields.name: active
plainFields.description: Whether the sanction is currently in effect. Used for runtime permission checks and automation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Time when the sanction record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Time of last update (status, end date, etc).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete marker (null unless deleted for audit).

models.name: discussion_board_notifications
models.description: Stores all notification events delivered to users for any workflow event in the system, including post/comment activity, sanctions, reports, moderation actions, or admin messages. Supports scalable, robust notification delivery to different user types (member, moderator, admin, guest if relevant). Ensures reliable, auditable delivery and user UX features like unread/read state, event linkage, and retention for compliance. Has foreign keys to relevant user tables depending on notification recipient type (using one Recipient ForeignKey per role; nullable for multi-type support), and supports linking to event entities (posts/comments/etc) in other domains by uuid reference only (no direct joins, preserving decoupling).

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Notified member's {@link discussion_board_members.id}. Null if not a member notification.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Notified moderator's {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}. Null if not a moderator notification.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Notified admin's {@link discussion_board_admins.id}. Null if not an admin notification.

foreignFields.name: guest_id
foreignFields.description: Notified guest's {@link discussion_board_guests.id}. Null if not a guest notification.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Notification title (localized for display). Required, typically under 100 characters for UI clarity.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Notification message content, including brief context or instruction. May be plain or rich-text, up to 1000 characters.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Business event type or workflow identifier for notification routing and category. E.g., 'post_comment', 'sanction', 'report_resolved', 'admin_announcement'.

plainFields.name: related_entity_id
plainFields.description: Event's primary entity id (e.g., post id, comment id) for routing and deep-linking. Not a foreign key, avoids tight coupling to other domains. Nullable if generic notification.

plainFields.name: related_entity_type
plainFields.description: Type/category of the entity this notification relates to, e.g. 'post', 'comment', 'report', 'system'. Used with related_entity_id for cross-entity notification routing.

plainFields.name: unread
plainFields.description: Whether the notification has not yet been marked as read by the user. Defaults to true (false when opened/read).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp (notification generated/delivered).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp (e.g., status/metadata change).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for retention/audit, null if not deleted.

models.name: discussion_board_permission_matrices
models.description: Stores normalized permission mappings for each role in the platform, supporting granular and policy-driven access control. Enables versioned changes to the permissions matrix, maintains audit fields for compliance, and supports soft deletion. Links internally to actor roles via string fields; referential integrity to user tables is managed through rule logs, not directly here.

plainFields.name: role_name
plainFields.description: Unique name of the system role this permission set applies to. Example: 'member', 'moderator', 'admin'.

plainFields.name: resource
plainFields.description: The resource this permission applies to (e.g., 'post', 'comment', 'report', 'category', 'policy').

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: The permitted action for this role over the resource. Example: 'read', 'write', 'delete', 'approve', 'review'.

plainFields.name: allowed
plainFields.description: Whether this action is allowed (true) or disallowed/denied (false) for this role-resource combination. Used for both allowlist and denylist patterns.

plainFields.name: effective_from
plainFields.description: Start datetime when this permission entry becomes effective (for versioning/time-based policy enforcement).

plainFields.name: effective_to
plainFields.description: Datetime when this permission entry ceases to be effective (null if currently valid).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation time for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update time for audit tracking.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp, if this matrix record is logically deleted.

models.name: discussion_board_rule_logs
models.description: Implements a complete versioned audit log for all rules and policy changes applied to the discussion board system. Captures rule type, full text, change type (created, modified, retired), and the operative system actor (by role and optional reference to a specific admin/member). Ensures roll-back, review, and compliance for all regulatory and internal policy needs. Designed for immutability once inserted, and includes full audit and soft-delete fields.

foreignFields.name: operator_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin user who enacted this rule change. References {@link discussion_board_admins.id}. May be null if operated by other role types.

foreignFields.name: operator_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member user who enacted this rule change. References {@link discussion_board_members.id}. May be null if operated by admin only or by system actor.

plainFields.name: rule_type
plainFields.description: Type/category of rule being logged. Example: 'permission_matrix', 'sanction_policy', 'category', 'general_policy'.

plainFields.name: rule_text
plainFields.description: Full text of the rule or policy document at the time of this change (snapshot for review/compliance).

plainFields.name: change_type
plainFields.description: Type of change for the audit trail: expected values 'created', 'modified', 'retired', 'imported', 'rolled_back'.

plainFields.name: change_description
plainFields.description: Brief description of what was changed and why (reason for rule modification).

plainFields.name: effective_from
plainFields.description: Datetime when this rule entry becomes effective.

plainFields.name: effective_to
plainFields.description: Datetime when this rule entry ceases to be effective (null if rule is currently active).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Audit field: time the rule log entry was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Audit field: time the rule log entry was last updated (should not change after initial write, but present for schema hygiene).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion field if rule log is deleted for legal or compliance reasons (rarely used).

models.name: discussion_board_external_auth_logs
models.description: Logs for all external authentication attempts (social login, OAuth2, email verification, etc.) capturing channel, external_user_id, subject email, key timestamps, and outcome. References discussion_board_members and related tables for identification. Provides audit trail for authentication-related issues and compliance tracing.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the authenticated member's {@link discussion_board_members.id}. Null if not mapped to a member.

plainFields.name: auth_channel
plainFields.description: External authentication channel (e.g., 'kakao', 'naver', 'google', 'email', etc.).

plainFields.name: external_user_id
plainFields.description: Unique user identifier received from the external provider, if applicable.

plainFields.name: subject_email
plainFields.description: Email address used in the authentication attempt (may differ from account email).

plainFields.name: issued_at
plainFields.description: Datetime at which the external auth event was initiated.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Datetime at which external auth flow was completed (success/fail).

plainFields.name: success
plainFields.description: Whether the authentication attempt succeeded.

plainFields.name: error_code
plainFields.description: Error code from external system or local process (if any).

plainFields.name: error_message
plainFields.description: Detailed error message or trouble context (if any).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp for the log entry.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for the log entry.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete marker for the log entry.

models.name: discussion_board_email_logs
models.description: Logs all outgoing emails sent by the system (e.g. verification, password reset, notifications). Tracks SMTP status, recipient, purpose, response data and integrations with external mail APIs. Used for compliance and troubleshooting outgoing communications.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member for whom the email was sent. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

plainFields.name: recipient_email
plainFields.description: Target recipient's email address.

plainFields.name: email_type
plainFields.description: Type/category of email (e.g., verification, password_reset, notification).

plainFields.name: subject
plainFields.description: Email subject line.

plainFields.name: sent_at
plainFields.description: Datetime email was sent (handed to mail server).

plainFields.name: delivery_status
plainFields.description: Status reported by the SMTP/mail provider (e.g., SENT, DELIVERED, FAILED).

plainFields.name: response_code
plainFields.description: SMTP or service provider response code (if available).

plainFields.name: response_message
plainFields.description: Provider's response message or delivery/trouble note.

plainFields.name: external_message_id
plainFields.description: External provider's assigned message ID for traceability (if any).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp for the log entry.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for the log entry.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete marker for the log entry.

models.name: discussion_board_ad_integration_logs
models.description: Logs for external ad/analytics integrations related to user activity and ad serving, supporting audit/compliance of third-party advertising or analytics data flows. Includes channel, event, response, and mapping to local events/users where allowed.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member associated with the ad/analytic event (if any). {@link discussion_board_members.id}

plainFields.name: ad_channel
plainFields.description: Ad/analytics platform channel (e.g., 'google_adsense', 'naver_ad', 'ga4', etc.).

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Type of ad/analytics event (e.g., impression, click, conversion, error, etc.).

plainFields.name: external_event_id
plainFields.description: Unique event ID as received from the external ad/analytics system, if any.

plainFields.name: local_event_context
plainFields.description: Context or description of the mapped local event (post viewed, ad clicked, page scrolled, etc.).

plainFields.name: event_at
plainFields.description: Datetime the ad/analytics event occurred or was logged by the system.

plainFields.name: success
plainFields.description: Whether the integration event was considered successful (versus error/fail).

plainFields.name: response_payload
plainFields.description: Raw response or request payload from ad/analytics provider (as string, often JSON).

plainFields.name: error_code
plainFields.description: External system or integration error code, if any.

plainFields.name: error_message
plainFields.description: Error/debug/troubleshooting context (if any).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp for the log entry.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for the log entry.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete marker for the log entry.

models.name: discussion_board_operation_logs
models.description: Records all privileged actions and high-impact changes within the discussionBoard platform (e.g., admin or moderator system actions, sensitive config edits, security events, high-importance manual interventions). Designed for immutable audit trailing, regulatory compliance, and forensic capability. References the user (admin, moderator, or member) who performed the action. Optionally links to the affected resource or target entity by UUID, without duplicating business data. Included fields support real-time and historical filtering of actions by actor, action type, resource, and time window.

foreignFields.name: actor_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Acting administrator's {@link discussion_board_admins.id}. Used when the operation was performed by an admin.

foreignFields.name: actor_moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Acting moderator's {@link discussion_board_moderators.id}. Used when the operation was performed by a moderator.

foreignFields.name: actor_member_id
foreignFields.description: Acting member's {@link discussion_board_members.id}, when a regular member triggers a log-worthy action (rare).

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of privileged operation or system action (e.g., 'user_sanction','policy_change','critical_config_edit','escalation','audit_view','manual_patch').

plainFields.name: resource_table
plainFields.description: Name of target resource table for the action (e.g., 'discussion_board_posts','discussion_board_policy_documents'). Allows generic linking to affected row, supporting polymorphism.

plainFields.name: resource_id
plainFields.description: UUID of the target resource row affected by this action, if any. Nullable to support system-wide actions with no single row target.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address (IPv4/IPv6) from which the operation originated. Used for compliance and forensic research.

plainFields.name: ua_string
plainFields.description: User agent or system identifier string for context (typically browser/OS or automation agent info).

plainFields.name: action_details
plainFields.description: Structured details or JSON (as string) containing the input payload, parameters, or contextual meta for the privileged action. For audit and forensic purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of log creation (UTC). Marks when the operation occurred.

models.name: discussion_board_policy_change_logs
models.description: Captures every administrative policy/config change in the discussionBoard system for legal and regulatory compliance. Stores before/after values, the specific policy/config target, actor, and justification. Ensures any change to governance, user rights, moderation, workflow, or audit policy is non-negotiably logged. Supports future audits, rollbacks, and incident investigations. Linked to the responsible admin and optionally references the previous policy revision.

foreignFields.name: actor_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator responsible for the policy change. References {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: previous_policy_change_id
foreignFields.description: Optional self-reference to previous version of this policy change log (for policy versioning/history). References {@link discussion_board_policy_change_logs.id}.

plainFields.name: policy_namespace
plainFields.description: Domain or subsystem of the policy/configuration (e.g., 'reporting','moderation','user_signup','permission_matrix'). Used for high-level filtering and classification.

plainFields.name: target_table
plainFields.description: Table name of the affected policy/config. Supports structured audit trails for adjustable policies.

plainFields.name: target_field
plainFields.description: Column or config key within the table/config that was changed.

plainFields.name: previous_value
plainFields.description: Serialized previous value (stringified or JSON as string) before the change, for rollback/audit.

plainFields.name: new_value
plainFields.description: Serialized new value (stringified or JSON as string) after the change.

plainFields.name: change_reason
plainFields.description: Justification, risk assessment, or change ticket/ISSUE reference for the policy update.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the policy change was performed and this log created.

models.name: discussion_board_post_metrics
models.description: Stores per-post analytics and performance counters, enabling trend tracking, operational dashboarding, and business KPI reporting for the discussion board. Each record reflects metrics for a single post and references the corresponding business post via a foreign key. Includes cumulative counters and snapshot efficiency data. Closely related models include {@link discussion_board_posts} (post entity reference) and dashboard aggregations.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_post_id
foreignFields.description: Related post's {@link discussion_board_posts.id}. Establishes which post these metrics correspond to.

plainFields.name: views_count
plainFields.description: Total number of times this post has been viewed. Used for popularity and reach analytics.

plainFields.name: comments_count
plainFields.description: Total number of comments on this post. Useful for engagement and discussion quality analysis.

plainFields.name: votes_up_count
plainFields.description: Total number of upvotes (recommendations) for this post. Measures positive community feedback.

plainFields.name: votes_down_count
plainFields.description: Total number of downvotes for this post. Indicates negative feedback or disagreement.

plainFields.name: reports_count
plainFields.description: Total number of reports (complaints) filed against this post. Used for monitoring community safety and moderation activity.

plainFields.name: last_activity_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent post-related activity (such as comment or vote). Aids in staleness/recency analytics.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Metric record creation timestamp (not the post's creation). Used for time series analysis of metric introduction.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last time the metrics for this post were updated or recalculated.

models.name: discussion_board_user_metrics
models.description: Aggregated user-level discussion board analytics, tracking each member's participation, reputation, and engagement trends. Useful for leaderboards, gamification, operational dashboards, and behavioral monitoring. References a member via a foreign key; all fields represent denormalized/cached counters for OLAP/reporting only (not transactional logic). Related entity: {@link discussion_board_members}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: User/member's {@link discussion_board_members.id}. Indicates which user's metrics are being tracked.

plainFields.name: posts_count
plainFields.description: Total number of posts created by the user. For gamification, leaderboard, and activity scoring.

plainFields.name: comments_count
plainFields.description: Total number of comments made by the user. Supports evaluation of engagement and contribution volume.

plainFields.name: votes_up_given_count
plainFields.description: Cumulative count of upvotes the user has cast (on posts/comments). Measures positive engagement impact.

plainFields.name: votes_down_given_count
plainFields.description: Cumulative count of downvotes given by the user. Tracks critical/judgemental participation.

plainFields.name: reports_made_count
plainFields.description: How many reports/complaints the user has filed. Supports abuse/oversight detection and moderation review.

plainFields.name: reputation_score
plainFields.description: User's computed reputation score, derived from post quality, votes, moderation status, etc. Reflects overall standing in the community.

plainFields.name: last_activity_at
plainFields.description: Last activity of the user (e.g., post, comment, vote). Useful for staleness detection, churn analysis, and award automation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this metric record was created (not the user's signup date). Used for metric evolution tracking.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last metric update for this user (not profile update). Supports scheduled batch recalculations.

models.name: discussion_board_daily_stats
models.description: Holds daily OLAP/cube-style aggregates for the discussion board (posts, comments, votes, reports, user signups, traffic, etc.) for business monitoring and executive reporting. Each record represents a single UTC date. Supports year-on-year/trend analytics, peak analysis, and real-time dashboarding. Not directly tied to a business entity, but cross-references multiple domains for time-based comparison.

plainFields.name: date_utc
plainFields.description: The UTC date (at midnight) for which all metrics in this record are aggregated. Used as the partition key for trending, comparison, and calendar OLAP.

plainFields.name: posts_count
plainFields.description: Number of new posts created on this calendar date. Used for engagement/traffic KPIs.

plainFields.name: comments_count
plainFields.description: Number of new comments created on this date. Tracks community interaction trends.

plainFields.name: votes_up_count
plainFields.description: Aggregate upvotes made across all posts and comments during the day. Measures positive activity trends.

plainFields.name: votes_down_count
plainFields.description: Aggregate downvotes made for all content types on this date. Tracks negative feedback.

plainFields.name: reports_count
plainFields.description: Total number of reports (posts/comments) filed for possible policy violation on this date.

plainFields.name: new_user_signups_count
plainFields.description: Number of new users registered on this date. For conversion and onboarding rate analytics.

plainFields.name: active_users_count
plainFields.description: Unique users who actively contributed (post/comment/vote) during the day. Vital for DAU/MAU and churn trends.

plainFields.name: traffic_sessions_count
plainFields.description: Total sessions (visits) recorded for the site/service on this date. Includes both members and guests. Foundation for traffic analytics/KPIs.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp (when this daily stat was first stored).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last batch/statistics update for this day.

/**
 * Client
**/

import * as runtime from './runtime/library.js';
import $Types = runtime.Types // general types
import $Public = runtime.Types.Public
import $Utils = runtime.Types.Utils
import $Extensions = runtime.Types.Extensions
import $Result = runtime.Types.Result

export type PrismaPromise<T> = $Public.PrismaPromise<T>


/**
 * Model discussion_board_platform_configs
 * Platform-wide configuration metadata for the discussionBoard service.
 * Used for storing system-wide settings, feature flags, and versioned
 * configurations. This table supports reference by all domain tables but is
 * never referenced itself. Rich description field supports documentation
 * and policy linkage. Designed for auditability and administrative
 * traceability.
 * 
 * @namespace Systematic
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussion_board_platform_configs = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussion_board_platform_configsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussion_board_categories
 * Hierarchical and dynamic topic classification master table. Each row
 * represents a configurable category for posts or comments, with optional
 * nesting via parent_id. Used by various content tables for topic
 * classification and filtering. Category data is editable only by admins,
 * and all changes are versioned via incremented 'version' field. The model
 * supports soft deletion and reordering.
 * 
 * @namespace Systematic
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussion_board_categories = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussion_board_categoriesPayload>
/**
 * Model discussion_board_policy_documents
 * Master table for storing policy documents, terms of use, and community
 * operational rules. Each record represents a single document (or version
 * thereof), and all policy changes are versioned for auditability. Used for
 * referencing within the application UI, linking to compliance, and
 * tracking user or admin acceptance. Document text is stored as full-text
 * for legal and search purposes; snapshot versioning allows robust audit
 * logs.
 * 
 * @namespace Systematic
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussion_board_policy_documents = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussion_board_policy_documentsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussion_board_guests
 * Non-member (guest) user tracking table. Records session or visitor tokens
 * for users accessing the discussion board without an account. Used for
 * analytics or tracking potential abuse, not for persistent identity.
 * Typically contains only anonymous access-related information (e.g.,
 * session tracking, legal policy audit logs). No foreign keys to other user
 * tables. No business fields that could identify a person are allowed. Only
 * operational metadata and temporal fields are included.
 * 
 * @namespace Actors
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussion_board_guests = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussion_board_guestsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussion_board_members
 * Discussion board regular member accounts. Stores essential identifying
 * and contact information for registered users authenticated via email or
 * social login. Includes profile management, core authentication (hashed
 * password for local accounts), email verification status, and role flags.
 * No foreign keys to other user role tables. All sensitive and personal
 * data adheres to legal privacy requirements. Audit trails ensured via
 * metadata fields.
 * 
 * @namespace Actors
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussion_board_members = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussion_board_membersPayload>
/**
 * Model discussion_board_moderators
 * Moderator role accounts for the discussion board. Moderators manage
 * content quality and enforce policy, with permissions above standard
 * members but below admins. May be promoted from members, but are tracked
 * separately here for audit and policy isolation. Includes information on
 * assignment and demotion periods. Only stores moderator-specific data.
 * Identity/authorization cross-referencing is via email (matched to
 * members) but foreign keys are not enforced to prevent privilege
 * escalation by join. Role change and status transitions are managed via
 * business logic.
 * 
 * @namespace Actors
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussion_board_moderators = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussion_board_moderatorsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussion_board_admins
 * Discussion board administrator accounts, representing the highest
 * privilege level in the system. Store critical admin identity and
 * assignment lifecycle details for policy governance and incident response.
 * No foreign keys to prevent privilege escalation. Assignment and
 * revocation are tracked with audit fields. All security-sensitive
 * operations logged elsewhere, but core admin info must be immutable and
 * auditable. Emails are used for login and communication, must be unique.
 * 
 * @namespace Actors
 * @author AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type discussion_board_admins = $Result.DefaultSelection<Prisma.$discussion_board_adminsPayload>
/**
 * Model discussion_board_posts
 * Represents all main forum posts in the discussion board. Each post is
 * authored by either a member, moderator, or admin (referenced via foreign
 * keys to those user tables) and is optionally linked to a
 * discussion_board_category and platform configuration. This table stores
 * only raw content (title, body, attachment link(s)), category assignment,
 * and status. No voting, comment, or moderation data is included here,
 * which are managed by other components. Includes temporal fields for full
 * audit (creation, update, soft deletion) and supports future extension for
 * post versioning and snapshot. Complies with 3NF, with no
 * denormalized/cached vote or comment counts.
 * 
 * @namespace Content

### `discussion_board_platform_configs`

Platform-wide configuration metadata for the discussionBoard service.
Used for storing system-wide settings, feature flags, and versioned
configurations. This table supports reference by all domain tables but is
never referenced itself. Rich description field supports documentation
and policy linkage. Designed for auditability and administrative
traceability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `config_name`
  > Unique system-wide configuration key name. Defines the purpose or area of
  > the config, e.g. 'feature_toggle', 'site_name', etc.
- `config_value`
  > Configuration value stored as text, interpreted by the platform according
  > to the config type. Can be JSON-encoded or primitive as needed.
- `description`
  > Human-readable explanation of the configuration's intent, affected areas,
  > and usage constraints. Useful for maintainers and auditors.
- `enabled`
  > Whether this configuration is currently active in the system. Supports
  > quick disabling/enabling of features or settings platform-wide.
- `version`
  > Version number for this config entry, incremented on each update for
  > auditability and rollback support.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this configuration entry was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this configuration entry was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this configuration entry was soft-deleted (if applicable).
  > Null if active.

### `discussion_board_categories`

Hierarchical and dynamic topic classification master table. Each row
represents a configurable category for posts or comments, with optional
nesting via parent_id. Used by various content tables for topic
classification and filtering. Category data is editable only by admins,
and all changes are versioned via incremented 'version' field. The model
supports soft deletion and reordering.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `parent_id`
  > Self-reference for parent category's {@link
  > discussion_board_categories.id}. Used to construct category hierarchies.
  > Nullable for root categories.
- `name`
  > Unique, human-readable category name as shown in UI and used for
  > filtering or search.
- `description`
  > Optional extended description of the category, for admin and UI tooltip
  > use.
- `display_order`
  > Integer value for sorting categories in the UI. Lower values appear
  > first; can be recalibrated by admins.
- `icon_uri`
  > URI to the representative icon for this category, used in front-end
  > navigation or list displays.
- `enabled`
  > Whether this category is displayed to end users and available for new
  > content assignment.
- `version`
  > Incrementing version for tracking category changes and enabling audit
  > trails or rollback.
- `created_at`: Timestamp the category was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp the category was last modified.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this category was deactivated or scheduled for removal.
  > Null if currently active.

### `discussion_board_policy_documents`

Master table for storing policy documents, terms of use, and community
operational rules. Each record represents a single document (or version
thereof), and all policy changes are versioned for auditability. Used for
referencing within the application UI, linking to compliance, and
tracking user or admin acceptance. Document text is stored as full-text
for legal and search purposes; snapshot versioning allows robust audit
logs.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `title`
  > Document title, e.g. 'Terms of Service', 'Content Guidelines', etc.
  > Unique for each simultaneously active version.
- `body`
  > Complete body text of the policy document, markdown or HTML-encoded.
  > Full-text search supported for legal discovery or compliance audit.
- `version`
  > Monotonic version number. Increments on every edit. Enables showing
  > current vs historical policy and supporting rollback/auditability.
- `is_active`
  > Whether this policy document version is currently in force and visible to
  > users. Multiple versions can exist; only one per (title) should be active
  > at a time.
- `created_by_admin_id`
  > Admin's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins) who authored, approved, or
  > updated this policy document.
- `created_at`: Document creation datetime.
- `updated_at`: Last modification datetime of the policy document.
- `deleted_at`
  > Datetime when this policy document was rendered obsolete or deleted. Null
  > if still current.

### `discussion_board_guests`

Non-member (guest) user tracking table. Records session or visitor tokens
for users accessing the discussion board without an account. Used for
analytics or tracking potential abuse, not for persistent identity.
Typically contains only anonymous access-related information (e.g.,
session tracking, legal policy audit logs). No foreign keys to other user
tables. No business fields that could identify a person are allowed. Only
operational metadata and temporal fields are included.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `session_token`
  > Anonymous guest session tracking token. Used to group activities from the
  > same device/browser during the same access period. Not personally
  > identifying.
- `last_seen_at`
  > Timestamp of guest's last activity. Used for analytics and session
  > expiration.
- `ip_address`
  > The IP address associated with the guest session for abuse monitoring and
  > operational analytics. Not for personal identification.
- `user_agent`
  > User agent string of the guest's browser/device, logged for audit and
  > abuse prevention.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the guest record was created.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest record was last updated. For auditing session
  > changes.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the guest session tracking was soft-deleted, if applicable.

### `discussion_board_members`

Discussion board regular member accounts. Stores essential identifying
and contact information for registered users authenticated via email or
social login. Includes profile management, core authentication (hashed
password for local accounts), email verification status, and role flags.
No foreign keys to other user role tables. All sensitive and personal
data adheres to legal privacy requirements. Audit trails ensured via
metadata fields.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Member's unique email address, the main login/account identifier.
  > Required for all members. Used for notification and password resets.
- `email_verified`
  > Whether the member's email has been verified for login and access
  > elevation.
- `password_hash`
  > Secure hash of the member's password, present only for local
  > authentication (not needed for external OAuth-only members).
- `nickname`
  > Display nickname for the member within the community. Unique within the
  > system.
- `avatar_uri`
  > URI to the member's avatar image. Optional; defaults to system image if
  > not set.
- `joined_at`: Timestamp of member's registration completion.
- `last_login_at`: Timestamp of last successful login for this member.
- `status`
  > Account status: e.g., 'active', 'suspended', 'pending_verification',
  > 'withdrawn'. String code, not enum, to allow for extensibility; enforced
  > by application/business logic.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the member record was created (audit trail).
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last update to this member (profile/account info changes).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp, set when the member requests account withdrawal or
  > is de-provisioned.

### `discussion_board_moderators`

Moderator role accounts for the discussion board. Moderators manage
content quality and enforce policy, with permissions above standard
members but below admins. May be promoted from members, but are tracked
separately here for audit and policy isolation. Includes information on
assignment and demotion periods. Only stores moderator-specific data.
Identity/authorization cross-referencing is via email (matched to
members) but foreign keys are not enforced to prevent privilege
escalation by join. Role change and status transitions are managed via
business logic.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Moderator's email. Used for correspondence and matching to member
  > accounts. Not a foreign key for strict separation of privilege.
- `assigned_by_admin_email`
  > Email of the admin who assigned the moderator role; for administrative
  > accountability and audit trail.
- `assigned_at`: Timestamp when the moderator assignment was granted.
- `revoked_at`: Timestamp when moderator rights were revoked, null if currently active.
- `status`
  > Moderator account status: e.g., 'active', 'revoked', 'suspended'.
  > Business logic enforces allowed values.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the moderator record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last update to this moderator assignment.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp for moderator record lifecycle management.

### `discussion_board_admins`

Discussion board administrator accounts, representing the highest
privilege level in the system. Store critical admin identity and
assignment lifecycle details for policy governance and incident response.
No foreign keys to prevent privilege escalation. Assignment and
revocation are tracked with audit fields. All security-sensitive
operations logged elsewhere, but core admin info must be immutable and
auditable. Emails are used for login and communication, must be unique.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`: Administrator's unique email address for login and communication.
- `assigned_at`
  > Timestamp when the admin role was assigned to this account. Used for
  > privilege lifetime tracking.
- `revoked_at`: Timestamp when this admin role was revoked, or null if active.
- `status`
  > Account status: e.g., 'active', 'revoked', 'suspended'. Policy and
  > lifecycle management uses this field.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the admin record was created (for auditability).
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last update to this admin record.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp for lifecycle management.

### `discussion_board_posts`

Represents all main forum posts in the discussion board. Each post is
authored by either a member, moderator, or admin (referenced via foreign
keys to those user tables) and is optionally linked to a
discussion_board_category and platform configuration. This table stores
only raw content (title, body, attachment link(s)), category assignment,
and status. No voting, comment, or moderation data is included here,
which are managed by other components. Includes temporal fields for full
audit (creation, update, soft deletion) and supports future extension for
post versioning and snapshot. Complies with 3NF, with no
denormalized/cached vote or comment counts.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `author_member_id`
  > Belonged member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). Used when post
  > author is a regular member.
- `author_moderator_id`
  > Belonged moderator's [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators). Used when
  > post author is a moderator.
- `author_admin_id`
  > Belonged admin's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins). Used when post
  > author is an administrator.
- `category_id`
  > Assigned post's category (optional). References {@link
  > discussion_board_categories.id}.
- `platform_config_id`
  > Platform configuration for post context (multi-instance/segmentation
  > support). References [discussion_board_platform_configs.id](#discussion_board_platform_configs).
- `title`: Post title. Maximum 100 characters. Required on all posts.
- `body`: Main post content/body. Maximum 4000 characters. Required field.
- `attachments`
  > Optional URI-encoded or JSON string listing post attachments (cloud link,
  > images, files, etc.). Up to 5 attachments allowed per post.
- `status`
  > Post status code: e.g., 'active', 'deleted', 'hidden', 'flagged'. Exact
  > codes managed by business rules. Used for workflow visibility and
  > moderation.
- `created_at`: Post creation timestamp (UTC).
- `updated_at`: Post last update timestamp (UTC).
- `deleted_at`: Post deletion timestamp (null if not deleted; soft delete logic).

### `discussion_board_comments`

Stores all comments (including replies) linked to discussion board posts.
Each comment is authored by either a member, moderator, or admin
(referenced via foreign keys to user tables). Parent-child relationships
are supported through the thread_parent_comment_id field to allow for
hierarchical reply trees (single parent per comment; top-level comments
have null parent). Every comment references its source post. Content,
visibility status, and temporal/audit columns are included. No cached
vote or report data is present in this table. Strict normalization: only
raw comment data and relationships are stored. Entity includes fields for
full temporal audit and soft delete. 3NF enforced; all denormalization is
prohibited except in mv_ prefixed views.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`: The post associated with this comment. [discussion_board_posts.id](#discussion_board_posts).
- `author_member_id`
  > Comment author's member reference if the author is a regular member.
  > [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members).
- `author_moderator_id`
  > Comment author's moderator reference (when a moderator authors; otherwise
  > null). [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators).
- `author_admin_id`
  > Comment author's admin reference (when an admin authors the comment;
  > otherwise null). [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins).
- `thread_parent_comment_id`
  > Self-referencing: parent comment's [discussion_board_comments.id](#discussion_board_comments).
  > Null if this is a top-level comment.
- `body`
  > Comment content/body text. Maximum 1000 characters. Required for all
  > comments (including replies).
- `status`
  > Current comment status: e.g., 'active', 'deleted', 'hidden', 'flagged'.
  > Statuses follow business workflow.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when comment was written (UTC, required).
- `updated_at`: Comment last updated timestamp (UTC, required).
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete field: timestamp of deletion, or null if not deleted.

### `discussion_board_post_votes`

Stores the record of each upvote or downvote by a member on an individual
post in the discussion board. Ensures that every voting interaction is
traceable, and a member may only vote once per post. Used for calculating
post popularity, abuse/fraud detection, and detailed interaction
analytics. Foreign keys link to the member (discussion_board_members) and
the target post (discussion_board_posts). All votes are auditable with
full temporal fields.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_post_id`

- `is_upvote`: Whether the vote is an upvote (true) or a downvote (false).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this vote was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this vote was last updated (e.g., for audit/toggling).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp for the vote interaction (null if active, set
  > when deleted).

### `discussion_board_comment_votes`

Stores the record of each upvote or downvote by a member on an individual
comment in the discussion board. Each record ensures that a member can
only vote once per comment. Used for calculating comment engagement,
community trust signals, and moderation/abuse detection. Links to the
member (discussion_board_members) and the comment
(discussion_board_comments). Auditable with full temporal fields for
forensics and analytics.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_comment_id`
  > Target comment's [discussion_board_comments.id](#discussion_board_comments) for which the vote
  > is cast.
- `discussion_board_member_id`: Voter's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members) who cast the vote.
- `is_upvote`: Whether the vote is an upvote (true) or a downvote (false).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this vote was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this vote was last updated (e.g., for audit/toggling).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp for the vote interaction (null if active, set
  > when deleted).

Relates to [discussion_board_posts](#discussion_board_posts), {@link

notification delivery to different user types (member, moderator, admin,

compliance. Has foreign keys to relevant user tables depending on
notification recipient type (using one Recipient ForeignKey per role;

Ensures roll-back, review, and compliance for all regulatory and internal

  > Datetime when this rule entry ceases to be effective (null if rule is
  > currently active).
- `created_at`: Audit field: time the rule log entry was created.
- `updated_at`
  > Audit field: time the rule log entry was last updated (should not change
  > after initial write, but present for schema hygiene).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion field if rule log is deleted for legal or compliance
  > reasons (rarely used).

### `discussion_board_external_auth_logs`

Logs for all external authentication attempts (social login, OAuth2,
email verification, etc.) capturing channel, external_user_id, subject
email, key timestamps, and outcome. References discussion_board_members
and related tables for identification. Provides audit trail for
authentication-related issues and compliance tracing.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > Reference to the authenticated member's {@link
  > discussion_board_members.id}. Null if not mapped to a member.
- `auth_channel`
  > External authentication channel (e.g., 'kakao', 'naver', 'google',
  > 'email', etc.).
- `external_user_id`: Unique user identifier received from the external provider, if applicable.
- `subject_email`
  > Email address used in the authentication attempt (may differ from account
  > email).
- `issued_at`: Datetime at which the external auth event was initiated.
- `completed_at`: Datetime at which external auth flow was completed (success/fail).
- `success`: Whether the authentication attempt succeeded.
- `error_code`: Error code from external system or local process (if any).
- `error_message`: Detailed error message or trouble context (if any).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for the log entry.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for the log entry.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete marker for the log entry.

### `discussion_board_email_logs`

Logs all outgoing emails sent by the system (e.g. verification, password
reset, notifications). Tracks SMTP status, recipient, purpose, response
data and integrations with external mail APIs. Used for compliance and
troubleshooting outgoing communications.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > Reference to the member for whom the email was sent. {@link
  > discussion_board_members.id}
- `recipient_email`: Target recipient's email address.
- `email_type`: Type/category of email (e.g., verification, password_reset, notification).
- `subject`: Email subject line.
- `sent_at`: Datetime email was sent (handed to mail server).
- `delivery_status`: Status reported by the SMTP/mail provider (e.g., SENT, DELIVERED, FAILED).
- `response_code`: SMTP or service provider response code (if available).
- `response_message`: Provider's response message or delivery/trouble note.
- `external_message_id`: External provider's assigned message ID for traceability (if any).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for the log entry.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for the log entry.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete marker for the log entry.

### `discussion_board_ad_integration_logs`

Logs for external ad/analytics integrations related to user activity and
ad serving, supporting audit/compliance of third-party advertising or
analytics data flows. Includes channel, event, response, and mapping to
local events/users where allowed.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > Reference to the member associated with the ad/analytic event (if any).
  > [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members)
- `ad_channel`
  > Ad/analytics platform channel (e.g., 'google_adsense', 'naver_ad', 'ga4',
  > etc.).
- `event_type`
  > Type of ad/analytics event (e.g., impression, click, conversion, error,
  > etc.).
- `external_event_id`: Unique event ID as received from the external ad/analytics system, if any.
- `local_event_context`
  > Context or description of the mapped local event (post viewed, ad
  > clicked, page scrolled, etc.).
- `event_at`: Datetime the ad/analytics event occurred or was logged by the system.
- `success`
  > Whether the integration event was considered successful (versus
  > error/fail).
- `response_payload`
  > Raw response or request payload from ad/analytics provider (as string,
  > often JSON).
- `error_code`: External system or integration error code, if any.
- `error_message`: Error/debug/troubleshooting context (if any).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for the log entry.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for the log entry.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete marker for the log entry.

### `discussion_board_operation_logs`

Records all privileged actions and high-impact changes within the
discussionBoard platform (e.g., admin or moderator system actions,
sensitive config edits, security events, high-importance manual
interventions). Designed for immutable audit trailing, regulatory
compliance, and forensic capability. References the user (admin,
moderator, or member) who performed the action. Optionally links to the
affected resource or target entity by UUID, without duplicating business
data. Included fields support real-time and historical filtering of
actions by actor, action type, resource, and time window.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `actor_admin_id`
  > Acting administrator's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins). Used when the
  > operation was performed by an admin.
- `actor_moderator_id`
  > Acting moderator's [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators). Used when the
  > operation was performed by a moderator.
- `actor_member_id`
  > Acting member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members), when a regular
  > member triggers a log-worthy action (rare).
- `action_type`
  > Type of privileged operation or system action (e.g.,
  > 'user_sanction','policy_change','critical_config_edit','escalation','audit_view','manual_patch').
- `resource_table`
  > Name of target resource table for the action (e.g.,
  > 'discussion_board_posts','discussion_board_policy_documents'). Allows
  > generic linking to affected row, supporting polymorphism.
- `resource_id`
  > UUID of the target resource row affected by this action, if any. Nullable
  > to support system-wide actions with no single row target.
- `ip_address`
  > IP address (IPv4/IPv6) from which the operation originated. Used for
  > compliance and forensic research.
- `ua_string`
  > User agent or system identifier string for context (typically browser/OS
  > or automation agent info).
- `action_details`
  > Structured details or JSON (as string) containing the input payload,
  > parameters, or contextual meta for the privileged action. For audit and
  > forensic purposes.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of log creation (UTC). Marks when the operation occurred.

### `discussion_board_policy_change_logs`

Captures every administrative policy/config change in the discussionBoard
system for legal and regulatory compliance. Stores before/after values,
the specific policy/config target, actor, and justification. Ensures any
change to governance, user rights, moderation, workflow, or audit policy
is non-negotiably logged. Supports future audits, rollbacks, and incident
investigations. Linked to the responsible admin and optionally references
the previous policy revision.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `actor_admin_id`
  > Administrator responsible for the policy change. References {@link
  > discussion_board_admins.id}.
- `previous_policy_change_id`
  > Optional self-reference to previous version of this policy change log
  > (for policy versioning/history). References {@link
  > discussion_board_policy_change_logs.id}.
- `policy_namespace`
  > Domain or subsystem of the policy/configuration (e.g.,
  > 'reporting','moderation','user_signup','permission_matrix'). Used for
  > high-level filtering and classification.
- `target_table`
  > Table name of the affected policy/config. Supports structured audit
  > trails for adjustable policies.
- `target_field`: Column or config key within the table/config that was changed.
- `previous_value`
  > Serialized previous value (stringified or JSON as string) before the
  > change, for rollback/audit.
- `new_value`: Serialized new value (stringified or JSON as string) after the change.
- `change_reason`
  > Justification, risk assessment, or change ticket/ISSUE reference for the
  > policy update.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the policy change was performed and this log created.

### `discussion_board_post_metrics`

Stores per-post analytics and performance counters, enabling trend
tracking, operational dashboarding, and business KPI reporting for the
discussion board. Each record reflects metrics for a single post and
references the corresponding business post via a foreign key. Includes
cumulative counters and snapshot efficiency data. Closely related models
include [discussion_board_posts](#discussion_board_posts) (post entity reference) and
dashboard aggregations.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_post_id`
  > Related post's [discussion_board_posts.id](#discussion_board_posts). Establishes which post
  > these metrics correspond to.
- `views_count`
  > Total number of times this post has been viewed. Used for popularity and
  > reach analytics.
- `comments_count`
  > Total number of comments on this post. Useful for engagement and
  > discussion quality analysis.
- `votes_up_count`
  > Total number of upvotes (recommendations) for this post. Measures
  > positive community feedback.
- `votes_down_count`
  > Total number of downvotes for this post. Indicates negative feedback or
  > disagreement.
- `reports_count`
  > Total number of reports (complaints) filed against this post. Used for
  > monitoring community safety and moderation activity.
- `last_activity_at`
  > Timestamp of the most recent post-related activity (such as comment or
  > vote). Aids in staleness/recency analytics.
- `created_at`
  > Metric record creation timestamp (not the post's creation). Used for time
  > series analysis of metric introduction.
- `updated_at`: Last time the metrics for this post were updated or recalculated.

### `discussion_board_user_metrics`

Aggregated user-level discussion board analytics, tracking each member's
participation, reputation, and engagement trends. Useful for
leaderboards, gamification, operational dashboards, and behavioral
monitoring. References a member via a foreign key; all fields represent
denormalized/cached counters for OLAP/reporting only (not transactional
logic). Related entity: [discussion_board_members](#discussion_board_members).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > User/member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members). Indicates which user's
  > metrics are being tracked.
- `posts_count`
  > Total number of posts created by the user. For gamification, leaderboard,
  > and activity scoring.
- `comments_count`
  > Total number of comments made by the user. Supports evaluation of
  > engagement and contribution volume.
- `votes_up_given_count`
  > Cumulative count of upvotes the user has cast (on posts/comments).
  > Measures positive engagement impact.
- `votes_down_given_count`
  > Cumulative count of downvotes given by the user. Tracks
  > critical/judgemental participation.
- `reports_made_count`
  > How many reports/complaints the user has filed. Supports abuse/oversight
  > detection and moderation review.
- `reputation_score`
  > User's computed reputation score, derived from post quality, votes,
  > moderation status, etc. Reflects overall standing in the community.
- `last_activity_at`
  > Last activity of the user (e.g., post, comment, vote). Useful for
  > staleness detection, churn analysis, and award automation.
- `created_at`
  > When this metric record was created (not the user's signup date). Used
  > for metric evolution tracking.
- `updated_at`
  > Last metric update for this user (not profile update). Supports scheduled
  > batch recalculations.

### `discussion_board_daily_stats`

Holds daily OLAP/cube-style aggregates for the discussion board (posts,
comments, votes, reports, user signups, traffic, etc.) for business
monitoring and executive reporting. Each record represents a single UTC
date. Supports year-on-year/trend analytics, peak analysis, and real-time
dashboarding. Not directly tied to a business entity, but
cross-references multiple domains for time-based comparison.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `date_utc`
  > The UTC date (at midnight) for which all metrics in this record are
  > aggregated. Used as the partition key for trending, comparison, and
  > calendar OLAP.
- `posts_count`
  > Number of new posts created on this calendar date. Used for
  > engagement/traffic KPIs.
- `comments_count`
  > Number of new comments created on this date. Tracks community interaction
  > trends.
- `votes_up_count`
  > Aggregate upvotes made across all posts and comments during the day.
  > Measures positive activity trends.
- `votes_down_count`
  > Aggregate downvotes made for all content types on this date. Tracks
  > negative feedback.
- `reports_count`
  > Total number of reports (posts/comments) filed for possible policy
  > violation on this date.
- `new_user_signups_count`
  > Number of new users registered on this date. For conversion and
  > onboarding rate analytics.
- `active_users_count`
  > Unique users who actively contributed (post/comment/vote) during the day.
  > Vital for DAU/MAU and churn trends.
- `traffic_sessions_count`
  > Total sessions (visits) recorded for the site/service on this date.
  > Includes both members and guests. Foundation for traffic analytics/KPIs.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp (when this daily stat was first stored).
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the last batch/statistics update for this day.

operations.specification:
Retrieve detailed information on a specific notification event within the political/economic discussion board. This operation fetches all fields from the IDiscussionBoardNotification entity, using the unique notificationId as a path parameter. Typically used to display the full notification detail and routing context (member/admin/moderator/guest recipient, event linkage, unread state, timestamps, and any associated workflow references) to the authenticated requestor. The data strictly mirrors the discussion_board_notifications schema, including nullable entity linkage and exact status.

Security note: Only recipients of the notification or platform admins may retrieve a given notification. Authorization logic should enforce access only by the relevant member, moderator, admin, or guest referenced in the notification's recipient columns. Retrieval does not mark the notification as read.

If notificationId corresponds to a deleted or inaccessible notification, a 404 error is returned. Relationships to related entities (e.g. post/comment/report) are delivered as UUID references. Requestors must have active session with role matching the recipient type (member/moderator/admin/guest).

This endpoint should be used in conjunction with paginated listing or search of notifications for advanced notification center workflows.
operations.description:
Fetches all available metadata and content of a single notification (by its primary ID) from the discussion_board_notifications table. Returns all columns from the entity, including title, body, event_type, unread status, recipient linkage (which may be member, moderator, admin, or guest), and timestamps for creation and update.

Access is strictly limited to the recipient user’s session (determined by JWT role and recipient column), or admins for audit/support. No data is revealed about notifications where the requestor is not the intended recipient.

If notificationId points to a soft-deleted notification, an error is returned instead of the entity. All lookups and enforcement rules are derived from the DB schema.

Standard error handling applies (404 for not found, 403 for unauthorized). This operation is closely related to notification list/search endpoints for mailbox or event notification display flows.

parameters.name: notificationId
parameters.description: UUID of the notification event to retrieve.

responseBody.description: Full notification detail matching the primary key, as per IDiscussionBoardNotification schema.

operations.specification:
Create a new notification event record in the discussion board system, storing content, event linkage, and intended recipient (member, moderator, admin, or guest, per DB schema). This operation inserts a row in the discussion_board_notifications table using the request data mapped to the IDiscussionBoardNotification.ICreate DTO.

Business use cases include workflow-driven notification triggers (e.g. on comment, report, post status, sanction, or system event). The operation supports setting title, body, event type, recipient, and optionally, entity linkage (by UUID and type) and unread status (default true at creation). Only platform business logic (not end-users) should invoke this endpoint—typically called by system or privileged code as part of a workflow or event handler. Audit fields populated automatically.

If input references an invalid user/customer/recipient or foreign key, validation fails. Supports only one recipient type per notification row (recipient member, moderator, admin, or guest, not multiple).
operations.description:
Creates a new notification in the discussion_board_notifications table for the specified recipient type (member/moderator/admin/guest) and event context. Fields map to the DB model: title, body, event_type, related_entity ID/type, and recipient foreign key. System logic ensures only one recipient column is set per notification, and event_type strings are validated per application domain rules.

Standard creation workflow: input is validated, required fields must be present (title, body, event_type, recipient), and the entity is inserted with unread flag set true. Timestamps and audit tracking handled by the system. Foreign key integrity and recipient role enforcement applied.

Errors arise on missing/invalid recipient or entity linkage; also ensures the caller has rights to create notification for target role. Designed for system or admin/moderator-initiated notifications, not for arbitrary user-issued alerts.

This operation supports updating the title, body, event type, recipient linkage, unread state, or related entity references (for example, for status change, correction or event context changes) using the IDiscussionBoardNotification.IUpdate DTO.

Permission enforcement ensures that only platform admins or the original system process that issued the notification may update notifications. Typically used for notification correction, unread/read toggling (for business-driven changes rather than user-side read), or for workflow-driven status updates. Fields not provided in the request are left unchanged. Success returns the updated notification. All updates are subject to database audit and field-level data validation. Hard/soft deletes use a separate endpoint.

Request will fail if the notification does not exist, is deleted, or the update violates role/recipient constraints.

Only authorized actors (admin, system process, or originator with sufficient rights) may modify a notification. Standard errors apply: 404 if the notification does not exist, 403 on unauthorized attempt, and 400 on failed validation.

Designed for administrative correction, workflow-based metadata update, or unread/read toggles. Audit trail for all changes is mandatory as per platform operation rules.

operations.specification:
Delete (soft-delete) a notification event from the discussion_board_notifications table, using primary key notificationId for lookup. This operation marks the notification as deleted by setting the deleted_at field, per DB schema. This prevents the notification from appearing in search/list endpoints and hides it from recipient UX. Only admin or system-level actors may issue delete; end-users or recipients cannot self-delete notification rows.

If the notificationId is not found or is already deleted, return 404. This operation does not affect application-level events beyond the notification, but soft-deleted notifications are retained for audit and recovery as per policy. Hard delete (physical removal) should only occur via background jobs or irreversible compliance purge.

Typical use cases: notification withdrawal, error correction, duplicate removal, or as part of compliance routines.
operations.description:
Soft-deletes the notification identified by notificationId by updating the deleted_at column in the discussion_board_notifications table. The entry will be excluded from normal user views and search APIs. Deletion is not permitted by the notification recipient, only system actors (admin) may invoke this operation.

If the notification does not exist or has been previously deleted, a not found error is returned. Soft-deletion ensures that historical or legal audit is preserved unless compliance-mandated purge is scheduled.

This operation is tightly related to notification lifecycle management in the discussion board application and should be audit-logged at the operation layer.

Returns paginated IPageIDiscussionBoardPermissionMatrix objects.

Direct mapping to the discussion_board_permission_matrices table. Each entry contains the role name, resource string, action, allowed/denied flag, and effective date period. Search supports filtering by role, resource, action type, and effectivity. Used in the admin console or policy editor to list or audit permissions. Security: only accessible to admin-level roles.

Interlinked with rule logs and policy editor UI, supports full RBAC policy management.

Used in the admin interface for RBAC management, audit, and compliance review. Only admin users may invoke this endpoint. Enforces security around viewing RBAC policies. Supports all fields for advanced search/display usecase.

Filter: only metrics records where 'last_activity_at' is before this timestamp.

last_activity_before.description: Filter: only metrics records where 'last_activity_at' is before this timestamp.

IDiscussionBoardUserMetric.IRequest.description: Request type for paginated, filtered, and sorted retrieval of user-level metrics records. All properties are optional except those affecting the desired result page/size. Follows the Prisma schema fields for 'discussion_board_user_metrics'.

IPageIDiscussionBoardUserMetric.description: Paginated result set for user-level discussion board metrics records. Includes page metadata and an array of user metric analytics entities.

id.description: Primary key for this user metric entity.

discussion_board_member_id.description: Foreign key for the member to whom these metrics belong.

posts_count.description: Number of posts created by this user.

comments_count.description: Number of comments made by this user.

votes_up_given_count.description: Cumulative total of upvotes (made by user on others' content).

votes_down_given_count.description: Cumulative total of downvotes made by this user.

reports_made_count.description: Number of reports (abuse/policy violations) submitted by this user.

reputation_score.description: User's computed reputation score, derived from engagement/activity/voting.

oneOf.description: Timestamp for user's most recent activity.
Timestamp for user's most recent activity.

last_activity_at.description: Timestamp for user's most recent activity.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this metric record was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this metric was last updated.

IDiscussionBoardUserMetric.description: Full user-level engagement/reputation analytics entity for discussion board members. Tracks cumulative post, comment, vote, report, and derived reputation counters.

discussion_board_member_id.description: User/member's foreign key UUID from 'discussion_board_members'.

posts_count.description: Posts count at analytics initialization (usually zero).

votes_up_given_count.description: Upvotes given by user at creation (defaults to zero for new).

votes_down_given_count.description: Downvotes given by user at creation (defaults to zero for new).

reports_made_count.description: Abuse reports made by this user at creation time.

reputation_score.description: Reputation score at onboarding or import.

oneOf.description: Timestamp of most recent user activity at analytics onboarding.
Timestamp of most recent user activity at analytics onboarding.

last_activity_at.description: Timestamp of most recent user activity at analytics onboarding.

IDiscussionBoardUserMetric.ICreate.description: Request body to create new user metric analytics record in 'discussion_board_user_metrics'. Used at onboarding or retroactive analytics import.

posts_count.description: Total number of posts to patch.

oneOf.description: Patch for user's last activity time.
Patch for user's last activity time.

last_activity_at.description: Patch for user's last activity time.

oneOf.description: Page number to retrieve in pagination. Optional; use null or omit for first page.
Page number to retrieve in pagination. Optional; use null or omit for first page.

page.description: Page number to retrieve in pagination. Optional; use null or omit for first page.

oneOf.description: Maximum number of items per page for pagination. Optional; defaulted by service.
Maximum number of items per page for pagination. Optional; defaulted by service.

order_by.description: Field to sort by, such as 'date_utc', 'posts_count', etc. Optional.

'asc' or 'desc' for result ordering direction. Optional.
'asc' or 'desc' for result ordering direction. Optional.

order_direction.description: 'asc' or 'desc' for result ordering direction. Optional.

date_from.description: Filter for start date (inclusive) in UTC.
